newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia not to release July trade data today.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia not to release July trade data today.

text.p: Malaysia will not release July trade data on Friday as the market was expecting, senior government officials told Reuters.
However, they did not say when the data will be released.
Malaysia's Statistics Department releases the trade data every month through the national news agency, Bernama.
The country's financial markets have been eagerly awaiting the figure to provide them with a fresh direction, particularly in the foreign exchange market.

In what analysts see as a monthly guessing game, the estimates for July trade balance have ranged from a surplus of 500 million ringgit to a deficit of one billion. A larger number of analysts said the figure would be a deficit.
However, economists have lowered their full year forecast for the country's trade deficit after a lower-than-expected first half figure.

In a poll by Reuters, economists from nine research houses said the trade deficit in 1996 would be an average 4.95 billion ringgit ($1.98 billion) against an average 8.55 billion ringgit they had predicted three months ago.
This compares with a trade gap of 9.2 billion ringgit last year.

The economists said the revision in the full year forecast followed a sharply lower trade deficit of 798.4 million ringgit in the first six months of the current year against a 5.6 billion gap in the corresponding period of last year.
